_meta.comment: Shared data for the EcoMeter extension and the Legerly pricing page. 'api' = per-token USD (input/output). 'subscriptions' = consumer plan $/month. 'free_tiers' = which models each platform's FREE plan exposes (drives the extension model picker). To update prices, edit the numbers here.
_meta.source: Official provider pricing pages + free-tier availability
_meta.verified: 2026-09-19 — FULL nine-provider re-read, the first since 2026-08-24, against platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, developers.openai.com/docs/pricing, ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, docs.x.ai/docs/models, api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing, mistral.ai/pricing/api, docs.perplexity.ai/getting-started/pricing, alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing, platform.moonshot.ai/docs/pricing and docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing. EXACTLY ONE RATE HAD MOVED, and it moved DOWN: DeepSeek cut its Flash model from $0.44/$1.32 to $0.30/$1.20 peak, and renamed it — the rate card now lists deepseek-flash (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) and states that deepseek-v4-flash is RETIRED, with legacy requests served by V4.1-Flash at the Flash price. Every other rate at all nine providers was unchanged, including both Gemini Flash promos ($0.75/$3.75 through 2026-12-31, then $1.50/$7.50, confirmed verbatim) and all four Anthropic families. TWO NEW ANTHROPIC MODELS added: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, both $10/$50, both carrying a 0.025x cache-hit multiplier where every other Claude model uses 0.1x. Z.AI's glm-5.3-flash promo EXPIRED on 2026-09-09 and was found ten days late: it is back at the standard $0.15/$0.50, confirmed against Z.ai's own rate card rather than trusting the figure we had recorded. GPT-5.6 Sol's $4/$20 now carries a promo block with standard:null — OpenAI says it is promotional 'at least through November 21, 2026' and does NOT say what it reverts to, and rule 3 forbids inventing the number. Perplexity's three Sonar rates now carry a machine-checked sunset for 2026-09-27, confirmed at source. Mistral's own pricing page badges Medium 3.5 and Large 3 as OPEN; both weights repos were loaded and both are now recorded, which makes the long-standing 'Mistral publishes only Small' claim wrong. Host spreads re-measured for all eight models with a hosted block.

caveats.claude-sonnet-5: $2/$10 per 1M is now the STANDARD rate. It launched as an introductory rate through 2026-08-31, and Anthropic's pricing page states the scheduled 2026-09-01 rise to $3/$15 will not occur. Resolved 2026-08-24 — no action needed at the end of August.
caveats._long_context: 'input'/'output' are the SHORT-CONTEXT rates. Where a provider charges more past a context threshold, the optional 'long' block holds { over, input, output }: 'over' is the INPUT-token count at which the higher rate starts, and that rate then applies to ALL tokens in the request, not just the excess. Thresholds are OpenAI >272k (per the tooltip on developers.openai.com/docs/pricing), Google >200k, xAI >=200k. Anthropic does not tier this way and has no 'long' block. A consumer that ignores 'long' silently undercounts long conversations by roughly 2x — which is the OPPOSITE direction to the unmodelled prompt-caching discount, so the two do not cancel out.
caveats._perplexity_request_fees: Sonar token rates are correct but they are not the whole bill. Perplexity also charges $5-$14 per 1,000 requests depending on model and search-context size. For chat-shaped usage that per-request fee typically exceeds the token cost, so any Perplexity figure derived from this file is a substantial UNDERCOUNT.
caveats._claude_tokenizer: Anthropic states that Claude 4.7 and later (Opus 4.7/4.8/5, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5) use a newer tokenizer producing approximately 30% more tokens for the same text than Sonnet 4.6 and earlier. Identical text is therefore NOT an identical token count across providers or across Claude generations. Any cross-model cost comparison built on a fixed token count understates these models by roughly a third.
caveats._legacy_keys: grok-4 / grok-3 / grok-3-mini, deepseek-v3 / deepseek-r1, mistral-medium-3 / mistral-small-3 and gpt-4 / gpt-4-turbo are no longer listed on their providers' current pricing pages. They are retained at last-known rates because they remain selectable in the extension's model picker; treat those numbers as historical, not current. CORRECTED 2026-09-19: o1 was in this list and should not have been — it is still on developers.openai.com/docs/pricing at $15/$60, exactly the rate stored here, so it is current rather than legacy. gpt-4 and gpt-4-turbo really have gone from that page. Re-read the page before adding a model to this list; 'I did not find it' and 'it is not there' are different claims.
caveats._deepseek_increase_landed: DeepSeek has now moved its prices TWICE in a month, in opposite directions, and both are recorded here because the second only makes sense against the first. UP on 2026-08-24: v4-flash $0.14/$0.28 -> $0.44/$1.32 and v4-pro $0.435/$0.87 -> $1.32/$3.96 (peak), roughly 3x input and 4.5x output. DOWN on 2026-09-19: flash cut again to $0.30/$1.20 peak, a 32% input cut, while v4-pro held at $1.32/$3.96. The model behind the name also changed — the rate card now lists deepseek-flash (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) and states that deepseek-v4-flash is RETIRED, with legacy requests served by V4.1-Flash and billed at the Flash price. We keep the old key because it is a join key across five files and DeepSeek still accepts it; the display name is now 'DeepSeek Flash'. RANKING, re-run 2026-09-19 as the old version of this note demands: at $0.30/$1.20 the cheapest DeepSeek model blends to $0.525 per 1M at 3:1 in:out (was $0.66), so it is STILL third behind Mistral Small 4 ($0.262) and OpenAI's gpt-5.6-luna ($0.45) — the cut narrowed the gap without closing it. Off-peak halves it to $0.263, which is second. The old note's closing claim that 'the cheapest input rate in the whole file is Z.ai's glm-5.3-flash at $0.075' is now wrong twice over: that promo expired on 2026-09-09 and reverted to $0.15, and the cheapest input rate in the file is $0.10, tied between gpt-4.1-nano and gemini-2.5-flash-lite. The lesson stands and has now caught itself: when a price moves, re-run every ranking the old price justified.
caveats._deepseek_peak_offpeak: DeepSeek meters by CLOCK TIME, which no other provider here does. Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Monday-Friday, EXCLUDING Chinese public holidays, which fall entirely into off-peak along with all weekend hours; every other hour is off-peak at half price. The rates stored above are the PEAK (undiscounted) rates, deliberately: off-peak is a discount you only get if your usage happens to fall outside a window you do not control, and quoting the cheap rate would understate the cost of the exact advice this project is most likely to give — 'drop your paid plan and pay per token'. Off-peak is exactly half of every figure stored. Re-read 2026-09-19: the windows are unchanged; the holiday exclusion was on the page and missing from this note.
caveats._promotional_rates: Some rates above are time-limited promotions, not standing prices, and they carry a machine-readable 'promo' block: { until, standard: { input, output } }. scripts/check-prices.js fails once 'until' is in the past, so an expired promo cannot quietly become a wrong price the way it nearly did with Sonnet 5. Currently: gemini-3.7-flash and gemini-3.6-flash are half price through 2026-12-31, reverting to $1.50/$7.50. Record the standard rate at the time you record the promo — going back to find it after expiry is how this data rots.
caveats._anthropic_fast_mode: Anthropic added a Fast mode (research preview) billing Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 at $10/$50 per 1M instead of $5/$25. Not modelled: it is an opt-in API service tier, like batch or caching, not the default rate a consumer pays. OpenAI renamed its equivalent 'priority' tier to 'Fast mode' on 2026-07-30; also not modelled.
caveats.deepseek-reasoner: DeepSeek's API aliases (deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner) track whichever model is current rather than a fixed version. Priced here as v4-flash and v4-pro respectively, which is an inference from DeepSeek's current lineup, not a published mapping.
caveats._open_weights: An 'open_weights' block means the weights are published and we have loaded the page they are on: { license, osi, params, url }. 'osi' is true only for a standard OSI-approved licence (Apache-2.0, MIT); it is FALSE for the bespoke licences the flagships carry, which are named after the model and must be read before use. Open weights is a property of a MODEL, not of a provider — Alibaba publishes weights for qwen3.8-27b and qwen3.8-2.4t-a95b but not for the qwen3.8-max and qwen3.8-flash tiers it sells alongside them, and Alibaba's own pricing page draws that line itself under a heading reading 'Text generation - Qwen (open source)'. Never badge a provider; badge the model.
caveats._hosted_spread: Where a model's weights are public, anyone can serve it, so the same model has many prices. The 'hosted' block records that spread as observed on OpenRouter on 'checked': n hosts, the cheapest and dearest, and how many undercut the model's own maker. 'input'/'output' remain the FIRST-PARTY list rate read from the lab's own page — the spread is context, not a replacement. TWO THINGS MAKE THIS LESS THAN LIKE-FOR-LIKE. (1) Hosts serve at different numeric precisions ('quant': int4, fp4, fp8, bf16, mxfp4). A 4-bit quantisation is a lossy compression of the weights, so the cheapest host is often not running the same computation as the dearest — the spread is partly a quality difference, not purely a margin difference. Most hosts do not state precision on their own pricing pages. THIS IS NOT UNIFORMLY TRUE: where the lab's own released checkpoint is already at these precisions, the hosts are running the published format rather than compressing it, and the block carries 'quant_native': true plus a 'quant_source' url proving it — the page then says 'served at the lab's own published precision' instead of 'precision varies'. Check the model's config.json before repeating the generic caveat; DeepSeek V4 ships fp8 with fp4 experts, so it earns the exemption and Kimi K3 (bf16 down to int4 across hosts) does not. (2) A host may list several SKUs for one model; we take the cheapest per host, so kimi-k2.7-code's first-party figure is the standard SKU, not the 'highspeed' one at double. Treat the range as indicative of a market, not as a like-for-like quote.
caveats._no_hosted_block: Three open-weight models deliberately carry open_weights but NO hosted block, and the absence is a measurement rather than an omission. The rule is n >= 2 DISTINCT HOSTS after collapsing each host to its cheapest SKU — one host is not a spread. deepseek-r1 has a single priced host. deepseek-v3 has three, but its stored rate is a retired last-known figure rather than a live price, so a comparison against it means nothing in either direction. mistral-small-4 LOST its spread on 2026-09-19: OpenRouter returns three endpoints for it and all three are Mistral itself ($0.15 twice, $0.165 once), where on 2026-08-29 Venice was also serving it as well. Apache-2.0 weights with no third-party host at all is a real and slightly surprising state for the one model Mistral actually opened — re-check it rather than assuming the block was dropped by mistake.
caveats._alibaba_tiering: Alibaba meters by INPUT-TOKEN COUNT with the tier rate applied to the whole request — the same semantics as the 'long' block above. All four models tracked here sit in a single 0-1M tier, so none carries a 'long' block, but other Qwen models on the same page have two or three tiers and would need one. Alibaba also prices the same model differently by region: qwen3.8-max is $2/$6 on the International tier and $1.65/$4.95 on Global. The International rate is stored, because that is the tab the page opens on and it matches the rate Alibaba charges through OpenRouter. One exception found: Alibaba's own OpenRouter listing for qwen3.8-27b is $0.425/$2.55, BELOW its published list price of $0.50/$3.00.
caveats._deepseek_open_market_undercuts_deepseek: The largest first-party-versus-host gap in the file, and it lands on the provider whose price moves this project already flagged. The weights are MIT, so the rest of the market never had to follow DeepSeek's 2026-08-24 rise — and did not. Re-measured 2026-09-19 against DeepSeek's newly CUT rate: ALL SIXTEEN hosts serving the model on OpenRouter are cheaper than DeepSeek's own API, the cheapest at $0.039 per 1M (StreamLake) against DeepSeek's $0.30 — a 7.7x gap on the identical published model. The dearest host of it, Azure at $0.21, is still below DeepSeek's own price. This SURVIVES the off-peak objection but no longer completely: at the off-peak $0.15 it is 12 of 16 rather than 16 of 16. Note the direction of travel — on 2026-08-29 it was 16 of 17 at $0.44 with a 6.5x gap, and DeepSeek cutting its price 32% still did not get it back inside its own open-weight market. Cloudflare, which matched DeepSeek's list price exactly in August, no longer serves this model at all. v4-pro is milder and does not survive off-peak: 6 of 15 at the peak rate, but only 2 of 15 off-peak, where StreamLake ($0.422) and Baidu ($0.431) remain below DeepSeek's $0.66 — the same two hosts as in August. The quantisation caveat is also WEAKER here than elsewhere: DeepSeek's own released checkpoint carries quantization_config.quant_method 'fp8' with expert_dtype 'fp4' (config.json, read 2026-08-29), so the fp8 and fp4 hosts are serving the format DeepSeek itself published rather than a lossy re-compression of it.
caveats._china_first_party_only: These three labs are priced from their own rate cards, read 2026-08-29: Alibaba Model Studio (alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing, JS-rendered — a plain fetch returns a shell with no prices), docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing, and platform.moonshot.ai/docs/pricing/{chat-k3,chat-k27-code}. Moonshot's docs serve a Markdown variant at the same path plus '.md', which is the reliable way to read them; three different pricing URLs there return a byte-identical SPA fallback if you guess the path.

promo.note: OpenAI's own pricing page states, directly under the flagship table, that "GPT-5.6 Sol's promotional pricing is available at least through November 21, 2026". It does NOT say what the rate reverts to, so `standard` is null rather than a guess. The last standard rate before this one was $5/$30 short-context and $10/$45 long, cut to $4/$20 and $8/$30 on 2026-08-24 — that is history, not a prediction, and must not be written into `standard` on the strength of it. "At least through" also means the date can move out as well as arrive, so re-read the page rather than acting on expiry alone. Recorded 2026-09-19; the gap was spotted on 2026-09-06 and left unactioned, and glm-5.3-flash then expired unnoticed for ten days, which is the argument for recording a promo even when the reverting figure is unknown.

open_weights.restriction: A 'Modified MIT' that FORBIDS rather than merely conditions: you are not authorised to exercise any rights under it if your company's (or your employer's) global consolidated monthly revenue exceeded $20M in the preceding month, and the bar applies to derivatives and combined works too. Above it you must buy a commercial licence from Mistral, granted at their sole discretion, or use their hosted service. The same licence NAME as Kimi K2.7 Code's and an opposite meaning — that one asks for a logo, this one closes the door. mistral.ai/pricing badges this model 'OPEN'. Read at source 2026-09-19.

sunset.what: Perplexity's Sonar chat-completions API is superseded by its Agent API; docs.perplexity.ai states 'Sonar Chat Completions is now Agent API. Sonar will be supported until September 27, 2026.' Confirmed at source 2026-09-19, date unchanged. The Agent API resells third-party frontier models at direct provider rates rather than pricing Perplexity's own Sonar models, so these three rates have no like-for-like successor and should be removed rather than re-pointed. Perplexity break-even no longer depends on them (see FRESHNESS A3) but they are still shown in the model table.

open_weights.restriction: The DeepSeek License Agreement v1.0 (23 October 2023) governs the weights; LICENSE-CODE in the same repo is MIT and governs only the code. Unlike the revenue-threshold licences elsewhere in this file, this one restricts WHAT YOU MAY DO rather than how big you may be: clause 5 imposes the use-based restrictions in Attachment A, which you must also pass on to your own users. No revenue or user threshold at all. Read at source 2026-09-19.

Free to use, sell and fine-tune, with TWO thresholds. Above 100M monthly active users or $20M monthly revenue you must display the model name prominently in your product's UI. Separately, if you run a Model-as-a-Service or 'AI Work Assistant' (coding / office-productivity) business and your group's revenue exceeds $50M over any 12 months, you must obtain a separate licence from Qwen before any commercial use; purely internal use is exempt from that second condition. Read at source 2026-09-19.

Free to use, sell and fine-tune. The only threshold is high: if you run a Model-as-a-Service business and your group's revenue exceeds $10 BILLION over any consecutive 12 months, you must pass a Z.AI security review — scope and method decided by Z.AI — before commercial use. For all but a handful of companies on earth this is effectively unrestricted, which makes it the loosest bespoke licence in this file. Read at source 2026-09-19.

Free to use, sell and fine-tune, but if you run a Model-as-a-Service business and your group's revenue exceeds $20M over any consecutive 12 months you must enter a separate agreement with Moonshot AI before any commercial use. A further clause requires prominent attribution above a usage threshold. That $20M bar is 500x lower than GLM-5.3's on otherwise near-identical wording — the same sentence structure, a wildly different practical effect. Read at source 2026-09-19.

A 'Modified MIT' whose only modification is ATTRIBUTION, not permission: above 100M monthly active users or $20M monthly revenue you must display 'Kimi K2.7 Code' prominently in your product's UI. Nothing is forbidden and no separate agreement is required. Recorded osi:false because a modified MIT is not MIT and OSI has approved no such licence — but this is the mildest restriction in the file, and materially different from Mistral Medium 3.5's identically-named licence. Read at source 2026-09-19.

anthropic.label: Claude
anthropic.note: Free plan: Sonnet 5 default (Sonnet 4.6 still selectable), limited Haiku 4.5. No Opus, Fable, or Mythos.

openai.label: ChatGPT
openai.note: Free plan: unlimited text chats on GPT-5.6 Luna (subject to abuse guardrails), plus Thinking Mini. GPT-5.5 has now FINISHED leaving the free tier — openai.com/chatgpt/pricing files it under "Legacy models" (Free: No, Go: No) and the Free Tier FAQ, updated 2026-08-13, lists only Luna. On 2026-08-08 that rollout was still in progress; it has completed. Free and Go get NO GPT-5.6 Sol at any reasoning level, and Terra only inside Work/Codex on desktop. Verified 2026-08-24.

google.label: Gemini
google.note: Free app: Gemini 3.6 Flash default, varying access to Gemini 3.1 Pro. Verified 2026-08-24 on gemini.google/subscriptions.

xai.label: Grok
xai.note: Free app runs Grok 4.6 — x.ai/pricing ticks Grok 4.6 in every column including Free, so xAI gates on rate limits, not model access. Verified 2026-08-24.

mistral.label: Mistral (Le Chat)
mistral.note: Free plan: Medium 3.5 and Small 4, ~25 messages/day.

perplexity.label: Perplexity
perplexity.note: Free plan: default Sonar, plus a ~$5/1k per-request search fee not shown here.

deepseek.label: DeepSeek
deepseek.note: Free web chat exposes the full model line-up (fair-use throttling only).

microsoft.label: Copilot
microsoft.note: Copilot resells OpenAI, but Microsoft publishes no model mapping for any consumer tier. Priced against GPT-5.5 as a stand-in only — not a disclosed mapping, and no API-equivalent cost is quoted for Copilot anywhere in the product.

zai.label: Z.ai
zai.note: Free chat at chat.z.ai runs GLM-5.3-Flash, per the Z.ai (Free) plan record of 2026-08-29. Login-walled, so no published message limits were found — the model comes from the product, the limits Z.ai does not disclose.
